local_articles.title: Kimi Antonelli hits wall as George Russell takes pol for Azerbaijan GP
local_articles.snippet: Kimi Antonelli was left ruing an uncharacteristic error in qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which eliminated the championship leader in the first session after he hit a wall in Baku. His Mercedes team-mate George Russell claimed pole with a fine lap and will be in a strong position to make up ground in the title chase in Saturday’s race. Antonelli leads Russell by 81 points in the world championship and has won the last two races but sat disconsolately trackside after only 11 minutes of running on Friday in Baku, when he was a little too eager into the 90-degree left-handed turn one and clipped the barrier. He took damage to the track rod and a puncture, and while he attempted to bring the car home, he was told to park up by his race engineer, Pete Bonnington. “We can’t fix this, mate,” he said. local_articles.title: george russell takes pole for azerbaijan grand prix
local_articles.snippet: BAKU, Azerbaijan – Briton George Russell stormed to a dominant pole position in qualifying on Sept 25 for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and saw his fading title hopes receive a much-needed boost from a crash for Mercedes championship-leading teammate Kimi Antonelli. The 28-year-old clocked a 1min 42.526sec lap around the 6km Baku street track, bettering his own previous benchmark by 0.5sec, to go 0.837 clear of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc. Australian Oscar Piastri was third for McLaren. Antonelli, who leads Russell by 81 points in the overall standings and came into the weekend gunning for his third successive win and ninth of the season, will start 16th after crashing out in the first phase of qualifying. local_articles.title: Verstappen denies Russell Azerbaijan practice clean sweep
local_articles.snippet: BAKU, Azerbaijan, Sept 25 - Four-times champion Max Verstappen denied Mercedes rival George Russell a clean sweep of practice for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by going fastest for Red Bull in Friday’s final session ahead of qualifying. The Dutchman clocked a one-minute, 43.922 second lap in the closing minutes of the hour-long session to pip Russell by 0.099 seconds. Lewis Hamilton also pulled out a late flier to go third for Ferrari 0.111 seconds off Verstappen’s pace. Runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who lost valuable track time to a hydraulics issue on Thursday, was fourth. Russell, who trails his 20-year-old Italian teammate by 81 points after 14 rounds, has looked dialled in all weekend.
